narrow_shared_operation_and_contract: Resolve request credentials and authenticate a session, subject to route-specific credential constraints.
rationale: Both resolve current/legacy/dev cookies and call authenticateToken; raw token verification already has an owner. Browser resolution independently reproduces a subset of request credential selection, but differs on Authorization precedence and proof binding. A shared credential-resolution policy might prevent drift only if those differences are deliberately modeled.
legitimate_variations: General request accepts selected cookie/bearer/DPoP and validates proofs; browser reads cookies directly and requires browser method with no proof key. General dev fallback is suppressed by any Authorization header; browser direct selection is not.
existing_shared_owner_or_delegation: authenticateToken already owns session verification, error mapping, audience rejection and projection; general path also calls selectRequestCredential.
uncertainty_and_disagreement: Cannot infer that browser endpoint should adopt general precedence or DPoP behavior. Narrow resolution overlap is real, equivalence is not established.
